MECHANISM_METHODS: The new fixed sensitivity compared full refitting, one common RMS normalization per trial, diagonal-reference alignment and full-covariance EA. Every Kumar arm used the same 21-dimensional Helmert common-average coordinates, four-component CSP with Ledoit–Wolf regularization (`norm_trace=False`, full rank), and automatic-shrinkage LDA. The BNCI arms retained the original 22-channel NumPy core and 0.1 covariance/LDA shrinkage. Diagonal references were defined in those fixed coordinates; Kumar contrasts are not individual electrode scales. These four arms required 396 new classical target fits. They saved genuine right-class probabilities and fitted-state digests before/after prediction. Balanced negative log likelihood used class-equal weights and a 10\(^{-7}\) clipping floor; binary Brier used the single-coordinate squared-probability definition.
PHASE_EXTENSION_METHODS: The EA phase extension used common eligible trial identities in cue-anchored 5 s and task-start 2 s pipelines. Source training remained 40 examples; in the nine-person conditional scope, each session retained 4–19 support and 5–57 query examples. Support/query counts and identities were the same between windows, but this was not the original 19/20-label complete-query endpoint. All source, support and query windows used the corresponding signal definition. EA used the original 21-dimensional whitening/re-embedding into 22 channels and CSP/LDA path; original full-refit predictions were replayed after identity checks. There were 148 new EA phase fits and 32 original undefined cells. Nine original primary participants had complete five-session endpoints; a metadata-complete sensitivity retained eight, excluding sub-15. Unknown markers and missing classes were retained as undefined.
MECHANISM_RESULTS:
With coordinates and decoder core matched, Kumar full/RMS/diagonal/EA BA was 65.36%, 69.52%, 67.88% and 70.43%, respectively (Figure 5). EA minus full was +5.07 [+2.88, +7.71] points. EA added +2.55 [+0.59, +4.49] points beyond diagonal alignment; its difference from common RMS normalization was +0.91 [-1.28, +3.18] points. The latter interval included zero. In BNCI, EA minus RMS was +4.63 [+1.94, +7.96] and EA minus diagonal alignment +4.91 [+1.94, +8.24] points. These new shared-core estimates remain separate from historical results.

In the matched fits, BNCI EA-minus-full balanced NLL changed by −0.07265 nats (−0.16079 to −0.00720) and Brier by −0.02629 (−0.05188 to −0.00771). Kumar changes were +0.01859 nats (−0.04038 to 0.07941) and −0.00923 (−0.02739 to0.00717), respectively. Thus, the classification gain did not imply the same probability-score improvement in both datasets.
PHASE_EXTENSION_RESULTS: The phase comparison located a marked dependence on signal definition. In the same nine conditional participants, EA-minus-full was 7.85 points (3.04–13.66) for cue-anchored 5 s windows and 0.13 points (−1.40 to1.92) for task-start 2 s windows. Their participant-paired task-minus-cue difference was −7.73 points (−12.17 to −3.76). The eight-person metadata-complete analysis gave 7.55 and 0.53 points, with a paired change of −7.03 (−11.84 to −2.97). Source/support/query trial identities were matched between windows; the retained calibration range was 4–19 labels per session. This is a joint comparison of anchor, duration and local filtering boundaries in complete fitting/evaluation pipelines.
MECHANISM_INTERPRETATION:
The matched-coordinate comparison retained a 5.07-point Kumar EA increment over full refitting. Its mean exceeded diagonal alignment by 2.55 points, while the 0.91-point difference from common RMS normalization had an interval crossing zero. BNCI EA exceeded both simple controls. These findings identify which preprocessing contrasts are supported in each setting: full covariance information added value beyond diagonal scaling, while the Kumar RMS comparison leaves the extra contribution beyond one trial-wise scale uncertain. Probability scores likewise require their own endpoint: BNCI NLL and Brier improved, while the Kumar intervals spanned zero.

The paired window result is particularly informative for the task interpretation. EA's added gain was 7.85 points in the conditional cue-anchored pipeline and 0.13 points in its task-start counterpart, with a negative paired change. The same pattern in the metadata-complete subset places the observed contribution in the evaluated five-second definition. Source, support and query windows change jointly in anchor, duration and local filtering context; the contrast measures that complete signal-definition change.
SUPPLEMENT_MECHANISM_DETAILS:
The four fixed sensitivity arms were completed under the analysis plan committed at 13dd764. All use the original source training and full current-support identities, with no query reference fitting or parameter selection. The scope contains 18 Kumar participants×five target sessions×four arms and nine BNCI participants×four arms, totaling 396 new target fits. All 544 new fits in this revision include these 396 plus 148 additional EA phase fits; historical neural source models were not retrained. The complete execution history, including the operational stop and same-state continuation without repeating completed fits, remains in the repository receipts.

For Kumar, every arm first projects common-average signals into the same fixed 21×22 Helmert coordinates. Full refitting applies the unchanged CSP/LDA core to the source/support union. Common RMS divides each complete trial by one scalar equal to the square root of mean squared signal across coordinate/time; it changes amplitude information. Diagonal alignment estimates separate source/support mean covariance references and retains only their diagonals in the fixed Helmert coordinates. Full EA retains the full references. The Kumar reference estimate has no extra shrinkage; every arm then shares four-component MNE CSP, Ledoit–Wolf covariance regularization, `norm_trace=False`, full rank and LDA `lsqr`/automatic shrinkage.

BNCI retains the original 22-channel recorded-reference arrays and original fixed 0.1 covariance/LDA-shrinkage NumPy core. Source/support domain references use its fixed 0.1 shrinkage. Its diagonal entries therefore refer to the original channel coordinates; Kumar diagonals refer to Helmert contrasts. Source/support counts remain 40/19–20 in Kumar and 96/20 in BNCI. No cross-dataset preprocessing unification or hyperparameter grid was introduced.

SUPPLEMENT_PHASE_DETAILS:
This extension adds EA to the original paired phase protocol; it does not relabel the earlier three-action result as EA evidence. The original 40 source TRAIN identities, common eligible support/query identities and frozen full-refit outputs were checked before fitting EA. The corresponding cue5s/task2s signals were used for source training, current support and later query in each pipeline. EA retains the historical 21-dimensional reference whitening re-embedded into 22 channels and original CSP/LDA defaults, separately from the matched 21-dimensional experiment in Section S19.

There are 148 new successful EA phase fits across all defined participant/session/window cells. Thirty-two original undefined cells retain their missing-marker, missing-class or otherwise undefined status without fitting; no marker was imputed. Original full predictions were replayed from their saved archive rather than retrained. In the nine-person conditional primary scope, all cells have 40 source examples, 4–19 support trials and 5–57 query trials. Each cue/task pair shares trial identities and class counts. This reduced, variable support budget must not be described as the original complete 19/20-label endpoint.

The nine conditional participants are sub-2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14 and 15. The metadata-complete subset contains the same list except sub-15. Its sub-15/ses-5 endpoint has five common queries (two left, three right) and 19 unknown original query-phase mappings; the conditional result retains it, while the metadata-complete result follows the original exclusion. Sub-11/ses-4 lacks the right query class in this scope. Participants 16–18 lack the required online phase mapping. All identities, counts and undefined endpoints are preserved in the cell and phase participant tables.
